result.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?
result.summary: Self-distillation is an emerging approach that trains a model to imitate its own predictions when conditioned on privileged information, such as correct answers or environmental feedback. Recent methods have reported better sample efficiency and generalization than reinforcement learning (RL), but it remains unclear whether these gains extend beyond in-distribution evaluations and whether they stem from privileged distillation. In this paper, we revisit two representative methods, Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) and On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), across code, science, tool use, and math reasoning tasks. We find that their reported gains do not consistently generalize to unseen problems and are largely explained by overfitting or transferring existing reasoning behavior, rather than effectively using privileged information. Moreover, self-distillation gradients show weak alignment with policy gradients that directly optimize expected reward, questioning whether they provide an effective direction for policy improvement. Our experiments across Qwen3 models (1.7B-14B) and OLMo-3-7B suggest that effectively leveraging privileged information to improve reasoning remains an open challenge. Our code is available at https://github.com/sleepypandu/does-sd-improve-reasoning

AI.brief_summary: 论文重新检验 SDPO 与 OPSD 两种自我蒸馏方法（以特权信息为条件模仿自身预测），在代码、科学、工具调用与数学推理任务上发现其增益不能稳定泛化到未见问题，主要来自过拟合或已有推理行为的迁移，且自我蒸馏梯度与直接优化期望回报的策略梯度对齐很弱。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「特权信息是否真正被用于推理」的诊断与梯度—回报对齐分析，可供核查 LVR 中监督信号是否真正驱动 latent 内容参与答案、以及贡献分配方向是否有效，属可借鉴的训练与评价线索，但论文为纯文本推理，未涉及视觉状态。
